title: The Bhagavad Gita: The Song of the Lord
subtitle: As Sanjaya told it to the blind king

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: The bow Gandiva slips from my hand

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon; rim light only
scene.detail: COLD OPEN: the Gandiva slides through an open hand in slow motion against the saffron rim; it never lands in this shot; hard cut to black on 'hand'
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 1.30 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: DHRITARASHTRA
beats.say: O Sanjaya! What happened on the sacred battlefield of Kurukshetra when my people and the Pandavas gathered?

scene.setting: the blind king's hall at night, pillars lost in indigo dark
scene.lamp: black; a flint strike; a single oil lamp catches
scene.king: Dhritarashtra on a high throne, a backlit silhouette, face turned away from the flame
scene.sanjaya: Sanjaya standing beside the lamp, silhouette
scene.overlay: धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे · dharma-kṣhetre kuru-kṣhetre rises in thin gold above the lamp, then the English line as it is spoken
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 1.1 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: You cannot see, my king, so you ask me. Your sons stand on one side of that field; your brother's sons, the Pandavas, on the other. My people, you say, and the Pandavas. Even your question is divided.

scene.detail: shadow-theatre: the lamp throws two armies of shadow across the pillars, one on each side of the throne, and they part as Sanjaya says 'divided'; slow push in on the king's hand

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Before a single arrow flew, one man on that field let his bow fall. Why? By the sage Vyasa's grace, I will be your eyes. Listen.

scene.detail: a thin horizontal line of gold opens across the dark like an eyelid; through it, far off, a plain at first light and one small chariot between two armies

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: The Bhagavad Gita. The Song of the Lord.

scene.line: as Sanjaya told it to the blind king
scene.name: The Song of the Lord

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: A note on how we work. Every verse you see is shown with its chapter and verse, in a public domain translation named on screen. Where we add our own reading, it is marked as our note. The pictures are drawn in code, the voice is synthetic, and nothing here speaks for God.

scene.detail: the hall, the lamp steady; the narrator steps out of the story for a moment

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: One. Arjuna's despair.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Dawn on Kurukshetra: two armies, banners, elephants, chariots to the edge of sight. Old Bhishma, grandsire of both sides, blows his conch like a lion's roar.

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon
scene.detail: two armies on a plain under an indigo-to-saffron sky; banners, elephants, dust lit gold from below the horizon; on 'conch' a single great conch raised on the far side

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Arjuna is the finest archer of his age. Holding his reins is Krishna: his cousin, his friend, his charioteer. And, as you will hear, far more.

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon; the chariot black against the rim, gold rim light
scene.detail: first sight of the chariot in its place: four white horses, the pennant streaming; Krishna's silhouette lowers the conch Panchajanya as the line begins; Arjuna standing with the Gandiva bow and helmet; Krishna in front with the reins, crown and peacock feather catching the light; hold on the reins in his hands

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: Please draw up my chariot between the two armies.

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon
scene.detail: on the last word Krishna lifts the reins and the chariot rolls alone into the empty strip between the armies; dust; the horses' breath in the cold air
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 1.21 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: O Arjuna! Behold, these members of the family of Kuru are assembled.

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon
scene.detail: Krishna's raised hand sweeps across the opposing ranks
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 1.25 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: There, Arjuna noticed fathers, grandfathers, uncles, cousins, sons, grandsons, teachers, and friends.

scene.view: slow lateral track across the front rank
scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon
scene.detail: no faces: helmets, raised hands, banners, an old man's white beard in silhouette, a boy's small shield; each word of the list lands on a new silhouette
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 1.26 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: He came to face an enemy. He finds a family.

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon
scene.detail: one silhouette across the gap, an old teacher with a staff, lifts a hand in greeting

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: The bow Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns. I cannot remain still, for my mind is in tumult.

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon; cold
scene.detail: the cold-open shot, now in full: the bow tilts from the open hand, and this time it lands on the chariot floor
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 1.30 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: I do not crave victory, nor a kingdom, nor any pleasure. What would a kingdom, happiness, or life be to me?

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon; cold
scene.detail: Arjuna's silhouette turns away from the armies toward Krishna
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 1.32 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Having spoken thus, Arjuna sank into the seat of his chariot, discarding his bow and arrow, overwhelmed with grief in the midst of the armies.

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon; cold blue with a last edge of gold
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 1.47 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Two. The yoga of knowledge.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Krishna's answer is stern at first. In effect: stand up; this weakness is unworthy of you.

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon; hard side light
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 2.2-2.3

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: My heart is oppressed with pity, and my mind is confused as to what my duty is. Therefore, my Lord, tell me what is best for my spiritual welfare, for I am Your disciple. Please direct me, I pray.

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon; soft
scene.detail: Arjuna's silhouette looks up toward Krishna
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.7 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: A friend has become a teacher. Arjuna tells him he will not fight, and falls silent. And there, between the two armies, Krishna smiles.

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon; warm gold rises behind Krishna

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: There was never a time when I was not, nor you, nor these princes were not; there will never be a time when we shall cease to exist.

sa: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्
tr: na tvevāhaṁ jātu nāsaṁ na tvaṁ neme janādhipāḥ
na chaiva na bhaviṣhyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param
scene.en: There was never a time when I was not, nor you, nor these princes were not; there will never be a time when we shall cease to exist.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.12 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)
highlight: never a time when I was not

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: As a man discards his threadbare robes and puts on new ones, so the Spirit throws off its worn-out bodies and takes on fresh ones.

scene.detail: a threadbare saffron robe slips from a shoulder of pure light and falls; new cloth unfolds and is taken up; no body is ever shown, only the light inside the cloth
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.22 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: You have only the right to work, but none to the fruit of it. Let not the fruit of your action be your motive; nor be you enamored of inaction.

tr: karmaṇy-evādhikāras te mā phaleṣhu kadāchana
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stvakarmaṇi
scene.en: You have only the right to work, but none to the fruit of it. Let not the fruit of your action be your motive; nor be you enamored of inaction.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.47 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)
highlight: none to the fruit of it
nor be you enamored of inaction

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Then he describes a mind that stands still: one that draws in its senses as a tortoise draws in its limbs.

scene.detail: shallows at first light; a tortoise, gold-edged, draws in head and limbs one by one and becomes a smooth stone of light while the water moves around it
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 2.58

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: He attains peace into whom desires flow as rivers into the ocean, which, though brimming with water, remains ever the same; not he whom desires carry away.

scene.detail: aerial: many rivers, saffron with silt, pour into a vast still indigo sea whose horizon never moves
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.70 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: A sea that never rises. I wish you could see it, my king. Krishna has said that action is far below a mind fixed on the Divine; and still he tells Arjuna to fight.

scene.detail: the king's face stays in shadow; only the lamp moves
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 2.49

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Three. The yoga of action.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: My Lord! If wisdom is superior to action, why do you advise me to engage in this terrible fight?

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon
scene.detail: Arjuna's silhouette gestures at the armies
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 3.1 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: No one, Krishna answers, can stop acting:

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: He cannot remain inactive even for a moment, for the qualities of Nature will compel him to act, whether he wills it or not.

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon
scene.detail: nothing on the field is still: wind in a thousand banners, the horses' flanks rising and falling, dust turning in the light
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 3.5 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: In this world, people are fettered by their actions, unless they are performed as a sacrifice. Therefore, O Arjuna, let your actions be done without attachment, as a sacrifice only.

scene.detail: a fire altar before sunrise; hands of light offer grain, ghee, a flower into the flame; each offering rises as sparks that drift up and become the morning stars fading
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 3.9 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 4 · Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Four. Knowledge, and the renouncing of action.

scene.english: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
scene.name: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action

beats.movement: Chapter 4 · Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Then Krishna says something no charioteer could say: long ago, he taught this to Vivasvan, the Sun. Arjuna objects that Krishna was born in their own time.

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon; the glow of the unrisen sun directly behind Krishna, so he is outlined by it
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 4.1-4.4

beats.movement: Chapter 4 · Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: I have been born again and again, from time to time; thou too, O Arjuna! My births are known to me, but yours are unknown to you.

scene.detail: behind the chariot, faint concentric rings of light, like ripples, each one an age; never a figure
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 4.5 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 4 · Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: My king, the one who holds the reins against your sons remembers every one of his births.

scene.detail: the king turns his head toward Sanjaya for the first time

beats.movement: Chapter 4 · Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Whenever there is a decline of righteousness and an increase of unrighteousness, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.

sa: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
tr: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata
abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛijāmyaham
scene.en: Whenever there is a decline of righteousness and an increase of unrighteousness, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 4.7 · AFTER SWAMI SIVANANDA, 1949 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Five. Renunciation.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: At one moment, You praise renunciation of action; at another, You praise right action. Tell me truly, I pray, which of these is more conducive to my highest welfare?

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 5.1 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Both renunciation of action and the path of right action lead to the highest; however, right action is the better of the two.

scene.detail: two paths of light leave the chariot and meet again at the same far summit
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 5.2 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: He who dedicates his actions to the Spirit, without any personal attachment to them, is no more tainted by sin than the water lily is wetted by water.

scene.detail: rain on a temple tank; drops bead into pearls on a broad lotus leaf and roll off, leaving it dry and shining
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 5.10 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Six. Meditation.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: The wise man who has conquered his mind and is absorbed in the Self is like a lamp that does not flicker, as it stands sheltered from every wind.

scene.detail: a clay diya in a stone niche; outside the niche a storm tears at banners; inside, the flame stands perfectly straight
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 6.19 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: Verily, the mind is fickle and turbulent, obstinate, and strong; indeed, it is extremely difficult to control, like the wind.

scene.detail: the same niche: the wind finds the alcove and the flame thrashes, bending almost flat
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 6.34 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: It can be done, Krishna answers: with practice, and with letting go. Then Arjuna asks what becomes of one who tries, and fails.

scene.detail: the same niche after the wind: the diya has gone out; a thin thread of smoke
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 6.35-6.38

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: My beloved child! There is no destruction for him, either in this world or the next. No evil fate awaits him who treads the path of righteousness.

scene.detail: a hand of light relights the diya in the same niche; the flame stands straight again
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 6.40 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Seven. Knowledge and realisation.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Now Krishna turns from the seeker to himself: to what holds the whole world together.

scene.light: rose and saffron rim, brighter; sun still hidden; the light around Krishna slightly brighter than the sky

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: O Arjuna! There is nothing higher than Me; all is strung on Me like rows of pearls on a thread.

scene.detail: rows of pearls, each holding a tiny world (a river, a city, a star), strung on one thread of gold that is itself almost invisible
scene.overlay: सूत्रे मणिगणा इव · sūtre maṇi-gaṇā iva (from the corpus, 7.7 line 2) in a card corner
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 7.7 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: I am the fragrance of the earth, the brilliance of fire, the life force in all beings, and the austerity of ascetics.

scene.detail: first rain on dry earth; a fire's glow; breath in cold air; a seated ascetic as a far silhouette; the gold thread runs through each image
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 7.9 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Eight. The imperishable.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: how may those who have learned self-control come to the knowledge of Thee at the time of death?

scene.view: the battlefield seen from the chariot
scene.light: rose and saffron rim, brighter; sun still hidden
scene.detail: ten thousand spears at rest; a crow crossing the glow
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 8.2 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Whosoever, at the time of death, thinks only of Me and, thinking thus, leaves the body and goes forth, will assuredly know Me.

scene.justification: 8.5, with 8.9's 'Brilliant like the Sun, Beyond the reach of darkness'
scene.detail: a single small flame lifts from a lamp and rises, steady, until it is lost in a vast sun; the sun's disc turns, gains twelve spokes, and resolves into the chariot's own wheel (match cut back to the field)
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 8.5 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Therefore, always meditate on Me and fight; if your mind and reason are fixed on Me, you will surely come to Me.

tr: tasmāt sarveṣhu kāleṣhu mām anusmara yudhya cha
mayyarpita-mano-buddhir mām evaiṣhyasyasanśhayam
scene.en: Therefore, always meditate on Me and fight; if your mind and reason are fixed on Me, you will surely come to Me.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 8.7 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)
highlight: always meditate on Me and fight

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Meditate, and fight. But how, my king, in the middle of a war?

scene.detail: the king's head lifts a little

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Nine. The royal secret.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Whatever a person offers to Me, be it a leaf, flower, fruit, or water, I accept it, for it is offered with devotion and a pure mind.

scene.detail: four close shots on cupped hands of light: a tulsi leaf, a marigold, a small fruit, water poured from a brass lota; each is set down before a flame
scene.overlay: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं · patraṁ puṣhpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ (from the corpus, 9.26 line 1), each word lit with its offering
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 9.26 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: A leaf. A flower. A little water. Anyone on earth could bring him that.

scene.detail: a single marigold petal on the floor of the hall, in the lamplight

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you sacrifice and give, whatever austerities you practice, do all as an offering to Me.

scene.light: rose and saffron rim, brighter; sun still hidden
scene.detail: the fallen Gandiva on the chariot floor, lit for a moment as if it were an offering; no added words
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 9.27 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Ten. The divine glories.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Then, in effect, he names himself in the best of everything: among things that never move, the Himalaya; among rivers, the Ganges; among letters, A; and among secrets, silence.

scene.detail: four cuts: the Himalaya under the first glow; the Ganges at Varanasi with lamps on the water; the letter A (अ) drawn in gold; then a dark, silent sky with nothing in it
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 10.25, 10.31, 10.33, 10.38

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Whatever is glorious, excellent, beautiful, and mighty, be assured that it comes from a fragment of My splendor.

scene.detail: each glory is revealed as a single spark struck off one fire
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 10.41 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: I sustain this universe with only a small part of Myself.

tr: atha vā bahunaitena kiṁ jñātena tavārjuna
viṣhṭabhyāham idaṁ kṛitsnam ekānśhena sthito jagat
scene.en: I sustain this universe with only a small part of Myself.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 10.42 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)
highlight: only a small part of Myself

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Only a small part, my king. And now Arjuna wants to see the whole.

scene.detail: the light in the hall is about to change

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Eleven. The vision of the universal form.

scene.english: The Vision of the Universal Form
scene.name: The Vision of the Universal Form

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Yet, since you cannot see Me with mortal eyes, behold, I give you divine sight. Now, see the glory of My sovereignty.

scene.light: rose and saffron rim, brighter; sun still hidden; a line of gold opens across the frame, the same 'eyelid' as Sanjaya's sight in the prologue
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.8 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: My king, I have that same sight, the gift of the sage. So I saw it too.

scene.detail: Sanjaya's silhouette shields his eyes

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Could a thousand suns blaze forth together, it would be but a faint reflection of the radiance of the Lord God.

scene.detail: whiteout from the centre: a thousand points of sun igniting in rings until the frame is pure gold-white; no figure, no outline, ever
scene.overlay: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य · divi sūrya-sahasrasya (from the corpus, 11.12 line 1) in deep indigo over the white
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.12 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: I see You, infinite in form, with faces, eyes, and limbs everywhere; with no beginning, middle, or end.

scene.detail: galaxies, rivers, mountains, cities, flocks, all turning inside the light, folding into each other; 'faces, eyes and limbs' are never drawn: only multitudes of points of light
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.16 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Then the vision turns, my king. In that fire Arjuna sees your sons, and Bhishma, and Drona, rushing in.

scene.detail: the gold deepens to red; far below, the two armies on the field, tiny, streaming toward the light like sparks

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: As rivers in flood surge furiously towards the ocean, so these heroes, the greatest among men, fling themselves into Thy flaming mouths.

scene.detail: the rivers of chapter 2 return, but now they are rivers of sparks pouring into a sea of flame; no mouths drawn, only fire
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.28 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: Tell me then, who are You, who wears this dreadful form?

scene.detail: the light at its most overwhelming; a small dark silhouette of Arjuna, kneeling, at the bottom of the frame
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.31 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Krishna's answer begins with one word: kala. Time.

scene.detail: the light slows; a great wheel of seasons and stars turns behind everything

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: I have shown myself to you as the Destroyer who lays waste the world and whose purpose is destruction.

tr: kālo ’smi loka-kṣhaya-kṛit pravṛiddho
lokān samāhartum iha pravṛittaḥ
ṛite ’pi tvāṁ na bhaviṣhyanti sarve
ye ’vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣhu yodhāḥ
scene.en: I have shown myself to you as the Destroyer who lays waste the world and whose purpose is destruction.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.32 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: I have already doomed them. Be thou my instrument, Arjuna!

tr: tasmāt tvam uttiṣhṭha yaśho labhasva
jitvā śhatrūn bhuṅkṣhva rājyaṁ samṛiddham
mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva
nimitta-mātraṁ bhava savya-sāchin
scene.en: I have already doomed them. Be thou my instrument, Arjuna!
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.33 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Arjuna bows, trembling, again and again, and remembers every ordinary day beside this friend.

scene.light: gold just under the horizon; sky almost day; sun still hidden
scene.detail: the light softening; Arjuna's silhouette bowed low on the chariot floor

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: Whatever I have said to you in rashness, taking you only as a friend and addressing you as “O Krishna! O Yadava! O Friend!” in thoughtless familiarity, without understanding your greatness;

scene.detail: memories as faint gold silhouettes: two young men laughing by a river, a shared meal, a chariot race; no faces
scene.justification: 11.41-11.42 name jest, sport, repose, conversation and banquets
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.41 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: I ask for Your forgiveness for them all, O You Who are without equal!

scene.detail: the memories fade; Arjuna's silhouette, hands joined, inside the light
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.42 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: I rejoice that I have seen what no man has ever seen before; yet, O Lord! I am overwhelmed with fear. Please take on the form I know.

scene.detail: the light begins to draw in toward a single point at the front of the chariot
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.45 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Lord Shri Krishna showed Himself again in His accustomed form; and the Mighty Lord, in gentle tones, softly consoled him who had recently trembled with fear.

scene.light: gold just under the horizon; sky almost day; sun still hidden; the light gathers back into the familiar silhouette: the crown and peacock feather, the reins in his hand
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.50 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: Seeing You in Your gentle human form, my Lord, I am myself again, calm once more.

scene.light: gold just under the horizon; sky almost day; sun still hidden; soft
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.51 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 11 · The Vision of the Universal Form
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: The light is gone, my king. A charioteer again, the reins in his hands. But now Arjuna knows who holds them.

scene.detail: the king has not moved; his hand is open on the throne now

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Twelve. Devotion.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Arjuna asks which seeker is best. In effect, Krishna answers: fix your mind on me. If you cannot, practise. If you cannot practise, work for my sake. And if even that is too much, let go of the fruit of what you do.

scene.justification: 12.8-12.11: each verse offers an easier way if the last is too hard
scene.detail: ghat steps descending to a river before sunrise; a lamp on every step; each 'if you cannot' moves the camera one step lower, and every step is still lit
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 12.1, 12.8-12.11

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: He who does not harm the world, and whom the world cannot harm, who is not carried away by any impulse of joy, anger, or fear; such a one is My beloved.

sa: हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः
tr: yasmān nodvijate loko lokān nodvijate cha yaḥ
harṣhāmarṣha-bhayodvegair mukto yaḥ sa cha me priyaḥ
scene.en: He who does not harm the world, and whom the world cannot harm, who is not carried away by any impulse of joy, anger, or fear; such a one is My beloved.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 12.15 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 13 · The Field and Its Knower
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Thirteen. The field and its knower.

beats.movement: Chapter 13 · The Field and Its Knower
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Krishna calls the body kshetra, a field, and the one who knows it kshetrajna, the knower of the field. Kshetra, my king: the word that opened your question.

scene.detail: a ploughed field before sunrise, furrows, sprouting rice; over it, unmoving, a still point of light that watches; then the camera rises and the field becomes the battlefield of Kurukshetra
scene.overlay: धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे · dharma-kṣhetre kuru-kṣhetre, the opening words of 1.1, with क्षेत्र lit

beats.movement: Chapter 13 · The Field and Its Knower
beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: He who can see the Supreme Lord in all beings, the Imperishable amidst the perishable, he is the one who truly sees.

tr: samaṁ sarveṣhu bhūteṣhu tiṣhṭhantaṁ parameśhvaram
vinaśhyatsv avinaśhyantaṁ yaḥ paśhyati sa paśhyati
scene.en: He who can see the Supreme Lord in all beings, the Imperishable amidst the perishable, he is the one who truly sees.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 13.28 (13.27 IN 700-VERSE EDITIONS) · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 13 · The Field and Its Knower
beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Just as the one sun illuminates the entire world, so too does the Lord of the field (Supreme Self) illuminate the entire field, O Arjuna.

scene.detail: seen from far above the earth: one sun rises over the curve of the world and its light runs across it, field after field, river after river (a world apart from Kurukshetra's horizon, where the sun still waits)
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 13.34 (13.33 IN 700-VERSE EDITIONS) · AFTER SWAMI SIVANANDA, 1949 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 13 · The Field and Its Knower
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: But what ties the knower to the field? Krishna names three cords.

scene.light: gold just under the horizon; sky almost day; sun still hidden

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Fourteen. The three qualities.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Purity, passion, and ignorance are the qualities that the law of nature brings forth. They fetter the free spirit in all beings.

scene.detail: three lamps in a row in the dark: a clear white flame, a restless red flame, a dim smoking wick; fine threads of light run from each to a single bright point and hold it
scene.overlay: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति · sattvaṁ rajas tama iti (from the corpus, 14.5) in a card corner
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 14.5 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Sattva, rajas, tamas: a clear light, a restless flame, a heavy dark. All three can bind, he says, even the bright one. How, then, does anyone go free?

scene.detail: on 'even the bright one' the camera finds the thread tied to the white flame too

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: And he who serves Me alone, with unwavering devotion, shall overcome the Qualities and become one with the Eternal.

scene.detail: the three threads slacken and fall; the bright point rises free above all three lamps
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 14.26 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Fifteen. The supreme person.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Now he speaks of a tree that grows upside down: the sacred ashvattha, roots above, in the Highest, branches hanging into our world. It must be hewn down, he says, with the sharp axe of non-attachment.

scene.detail: a vast fig tree hangs from a sky of light, roots above, branches and leaves trailing down into a world of rivers and cities; on 'axe' a single clean stroke of light cuts through the trunk
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 15.1-15.3

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire shines there. Those who go there never come back. For, O Arjuna, that is my celestial home!

sa: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः।
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम
tr: na tad bhāsayate sūryo na śhaśhāṅko na pāvakaḥ
yad gatvā na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṁ mama
scene.en: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire shines there. Those who go there never come back. For, O Arjuna, that is my celestial home!
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 15.6 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)
highlight: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire shines there

beats.movement: Chapter 16 · The Divine and the Demonic
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Sixteen. The divine and the demonic.

beats.movement: Chapter 16 · The Divine and the Demonic
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Two roads. Along one, he names the divine qualities: fearlessness first, then truth, compassion, forgiveness, freedom from hate. Along the other: hypocrisy, pride, cruelty.

scene.detail: a road forks before sunrise: one climbs toward the glow, lined with small lamps; the other runs down into shadow; each named quality appears as a word in gold or in smoke along its road
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 16.1-16.4

beats.movement: Chapter 16 · The Divine and the Demonic
beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Godly qualities lead to liberation; godless ones lead to bondage. Do not be anxious, Prince! You have the Godly qualities.

scene.light: gold just under the horizon; sky almost day; sun still hidden; warm
scene.detail: Krishna's hand rests on Arjuna's shoulder in silhouette
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 16.5 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 16 · The Divine and the Demonic
beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: The gates of hell are three: lust, wrath, and avarice; they destroy the Self, so avoid them.

scene.detail: on the shadow road, three dark gateways one behind another; the chariot's road turns away from them toward the light
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 16.21 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 16 · The Divine and the Demonic
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Do not be anxious, he tells Arjuna. He will say it again, at the very end.

scene.light: gold just under the horizon; sky almost day; sun still hidden

beats.movement: Chapter 17 · The Three Kinds of Faith
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Seventeen. Three kinds of faith.

beats.movement: Chapter 17 · The Three Kinds of Faith
beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Every person's faith conforms to their nature. By nature, they are full of faith. They are, in fact, what their faith makes them.

scene.detail: the three lamps of chapter 14 return, now each held in a different pair of hands
scene.overlay: यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः · yo yach-chhraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ (from the corpus, 17.3 line 2) in a card corner
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 17.3 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 17 · The Three Kinds of Faith
beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Speech that hurts no one, that is true, pleasant to listen to, and beneficial, and the constant study of the scriptures—this is austerity of speech.

sa: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्।
tr: anudvega-karaṁ vākyaṁ satyaṁ priya-hitaṁ cha yat
svādhyāyābhyasanaṁ chaiva vāṅ-mayaṁ tapa uchyate
scene.en: Speech that hurts no one, that is true, pleasant to listen to, and beneficial, and the constant study of the scriptures—this is austerity of speech.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 17.15 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.movement: Chapter 17 · The Three Kinds of Faith
beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: And he names the Eternal in three syllables. Om. Tat. Sat.

scene.detail: ॐ तत् सत् written in gold fire above an altar flame, one syllable per word spoken
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 17.23

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Eighteen. Liberation.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: The last chapter, my king. Arjuna asks what it truly means to renounce.

scene.light: rim burning white-gold; sun about to break; the armies still waiting

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: The sages say that renunciation is forgoing an action that springs from desire, and relinquishing is the surrender of its fruit.

sa: काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः।
tr: kāmyānāṁ karmaṇāṁ nyāsaṁ sannyāsaṁ kavayo viduḥ
sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṁ prāhus tyāgaṁ vichakṣhaṇāḥ
scene.en: The sages say that renunciation is forgoing an action that springs from desire, and relinquishing is the surrender of its fruit.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.2 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)
highlight: relinquishing is the surrender of its fruit

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: The duty that falls to one's lot of its own accord should not be abandoned, though it may have its defects. All acts are marred by defects, just as fire is obscured by smoke.

scene.detail: a fire on open ground, smoke curling over it; wind clears the smoke for a moment and the fire is whole and bright beneath
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.48 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Thus, I have revealed to you the truth, the mystery of mysteries. Having thought it over, you are free to act as you wish.

tr: iti te jñānam ākhyātaṁ guhyād guhyataraṁ mayā
vimṛiśhyaitad aśheṣheṇa yathechchhasi tathā kuru
scene.en: Thus, I have revealed to you the truth, the mystery of mysteries. Having thought it over, you are free to act as you wish.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.63 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)
highlight: you are free to act as you wish

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Free, my king. After everything, he leaves the choice to Arjuna. And then he speaks once more, as a friend.

scene.detail: the king lifts his face toward the voice

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Listen to My last word once more, the deepest secret of all; you are My beloved, you are My friend, and I speak for your welfare.

scene.light: rim burning white-gold; sun about to break; the warmest light of the film
scene.detail: Krishna turned fully to Arjuna; the reins slack in one hand
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.64 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Give up your earthly duties, surrender yourself to Me alone. Do not be anxious; I will absolve you from all your sins.

sa: अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः
tr: sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śharaṇaṁ vraja
ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣhayiṣhyāmi mā śhuchaḥ
scene.en: Give up your earthly duties, surrender yourself to Me alone. Do not be anxious; I will absolve you from all your sins.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.66 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: O Arjuna, have you listened attentively to My words? Has your ignorance and delusion gone?

scene.light: rim burning white-gold; sun about to break
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.72 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: My Lord! O Immutable One! My delusion has fled. By Your Grace, O Changeless One, the light has dawned. My doubts have been dispelled, and I stand before You ready to do Your will.

scene.light: the disc of the sun clears the horizon for the first time in the film, exactly on 'the light has dawned'; gold floods the field
scene.detail: Arjuna rises and lifts the Gandiva from the chariot floor; on 'ready to do Your will' it is raised into the sun
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.73 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: As I recall again and again the exceeding beauty of the Lord, I am filled with amazement and joy.

scene.detail: first grey of morning at the high windows; a faint gold afterglow of the thousand suns on Sanjaya's silhouette
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.77 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: You asked me what happened on that field, my king. You have not said a word since.

scene.detail: the king's silhouette, very still

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Wherever Lord Shri Krishna, the Prince of Wisdom, and Arjuna, the Great Archer, are, I am certain that good fortune, victory, happiness, and righteousness will follow.

sa: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः।
tr: yatra yogeśhvaraḥ kṛiṣhṇo yatra pārtho dhanur-dharaḥ
tatra śhrīr vijayo bhūtir dhruvā nītir matir mama
scene.en: Wherever Lord Shri Krishna, the Prince of Wisdom, and Arjuna, the Great Archer, are, I am certain that good fortune, victory, happiness, and righteousness will follow.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.78 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)
highlight: good fortune, victory, happiness, and righteousness

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Eighteen chapters. Seven hundred verses. One conversation between two friends; and one of them held the reins.

scene.light: full morning sun over Kurukshetra
scene.detail: the chariot between the armies in full sunlight: four white horses, the pennant streaming, Arjuna standing with the bow raised, Krishna at the reins

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: This was the Bhagavad Gita, as Sanjaya told it to the blind king.

lines: The Bhagavad Gita, as Sanjaya told it
